# Exploratory follow-up of 13.11.2026 (course folder pro/followup-2026-11-12/results.md). Not in the plan;
# decides no hypothesis.
#
# The sum control that sampling_large.toml lacks: target_sum_xx with all columns tried at each split
# (max_features = 1.0), six large datasets, 16,000 training rows, seed 0, outer folds 0-2. 18 tasks.
# NOT a blind test: a reviewer's diagnostic (fit_predict called directly, same pairs) already gave sums +6.0%
# against base on sgemm, more than the products' +4.4%. This run makes that an official result.
# Question, as in large_content.toml (LC1): with all columns, does target_xx (sampling_large.toml) beat
# target_sum_xx in all 3 folds? Expected from the diagnostic: no on sgemm and covertype, yes on higgs_low.
datasets = ["covertype", "miniboone", "higgs", "higgs_low", "sgemm", "casp"]
seeds = [0]
outer_folds = 5

[[check]]
name = "all_n16000"
methods = ["target_sum_xx"]
cascade = { train_rows = 16000, max_features = 1.0 }
